message:
Fingertip touch is covered from skin to hand but two functions have no real choice and two statements are still owed. Plain words: the soft dome, the hard bone, the two-signal touch feel, the spot sharing location, the fast shake warning and the finger computer are selected, yet transmission has only one path and conforming has only skin ideas from one specialist. The numbers that decide cover are six functions with two members with real alternatives in four functions, zero real alternatives in the transmit tactile message function with only the on-finger readout concept (C22) and in the conform contact surface function with only molded dome ideas from Dr. Amara Okafor, and Dr. Marcus Reid still owes a none statement for conform contact surface and for transduce contact stress, so the two weakest functions are transmit tactile message for Dr. Marcus Reid and Dr. Elena Vasquez and conform contact surface for Dr. Amara Okafor and Prof. Kenji Tanaka to each bring one distant analogy with written mapping in cycle 2, and the critical quantity nobody computed is signal margin and saturation from light touch to full grip.

Everyday touch checks pass for gentle contact but the small electrical change looks too small and the size and weight add up near a real fingertip. Plain words: a grain of sand touch spreads to a tiny spot at gentle pressure, the fingertip stays finger sized and spoon light on little power, and the fast warning fits inside human reflex, all familiar scales. The numbers that decide it are 0.102 g weight feel at 1.00 mN spreading to 0.470 mm diameter spot at 5.78 kPa in the Hertz spot size (E14), 20.0 mm diameter by 22.0 mm long staying inside the 26 by 20 by 25 mm precedent in the BioTac Product Manual (E43), 14.0 g total in the mass budget sum (E53) against 9.50 g precedent which is about one and a half teaspoons and still finger scale, 0.0991 W in the power budget sum (E51) about one tenth of a small lamp, 30.0 ms warning inside 43.2 ms from micro-slip at 53.6 ms to gross slip at 96.8 ms in the stick to slip simulation (E38), reconciled ridge tone at 125 Hz from 0.400 mm pitch at 50.0 mm per s correcting the 8.00 s unit slip in the ridge frequency calculation (E39), and the 3.57 attofarad change in the delta capacitance calculation (E28) sitting about two hundred times below femtofarad converter resolution which is outside everyday electronics comfort and must be fixed.

No open blocking objection stops the device and no readiness vote asks to build yet. Plain words: the board holds no blocking objection, and all four not ready votes point to the same missing proof that the tiny touch survives to the hand in time. The numbers that decide it are zero blocking objections on the board, 2200 Hz sampling with 30.0 ms window from the BioTac slip chapter (E31), 9.00 ms converter update in the converter datasheet (E41) and 51.2 kbit per s message rate (E52), so Dr. Amara Okafor is answered by keeping her thin stack under 2.50 mm, Prof. Kenji Tanaka is answered by requiring proof his attofarad signal clears noise and crosstalk, Dr. Elena Vasquez is answered by requiring shear plus vibration on hardware timing, and Dr. Marcus Reid is answered by requiring continuity and processor load as bench tests.

RECORD: Decided selections are molded Shore A 10 dome with fingerprint ridges for conform, nail-backed core with screw plus dovetail for support, capacitive taxels plus Polyvinylidene Fluoride, where Polyvinylidene Fluoride means PVDF vibration film, for transduce, 2.00 mm pitch grid with centroid for location, vibration power plus shear check for slip, on-finger Capacitance-to-Digital Converter, where Capacitance-to-Digital Converter means CDC, plus Microcontroller Unit, where Microcontroller Unit means MCU, with Serial Peripheral Interface, where Serial Peripheral Interface means SPI, for transmit; numbers that stand are 0.470 mm spot at 5.78 kPa (E14), 0.269 pF base (E26) with 3.57 aF change (E28), 125 Hz ridge tone (E39 corrected), 53.6 ms to 96.8 ms slip gap with 30.0 ms window (E38), 14.0 g mass (E53), 0.0991 W power (E51), 51.2 kbit per s rate (E52), 20.0 mm by 22.0 mm size; still open are transmit redundancy and conform alternative with analogies owed by Dr. Marcus Reid with Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Amara Okafor with Prof. Kenji Tanaka, none statements owed by Dr. Marcus Reid for F1 and F3, and signal margin plus saturation plus timing bench tests owed by Prof. Kenji Tanaka with Dr. Marcus Reid and Dr. Elena Vasquez with Dr. Marcus Reid.
Note on Dr. Amara Okafor: quantified gentle touch spreading and set thin stack and ridge rules that others can build on.
Note on Prof. Kenji Tanaka: turned pressure into capacitance numbers and pitch rules but signal sits below converter comfort.
Note on Dr. Elena Vasquez: separated fast slip shake from steady push and set sampling and timing that fits human reflex.
Note on Dr. Marcus Reid: gave bone mount plus finger computer path with size weight power sums near proven precedent.
My position: not ready, because the attofarad margin, full grip saturation, and timed hardware proof are still missing.
